reading.title: A Table for Quiet Reading
reading.text:
Our school library is small. After lunch, some students read there, but others talk about their games. Mia likes reading stories, yet she often loses her place when people speak loudly.

On Monday, she tells Mr Lee about the problem. He does not ask everyone to leave. Instead, he puts a blue card on one table near the window. The card says, "Quiet reading here." Students can still talk softly at the other tables.

Mia makes a small box for bookmarks. Anyone at the blue-card table can borrow one and return it before leaving. On Friday, six students sit at the table. One boy is reading his first story in English. "I can understand it better here," he says.

Mia is happy. She has not made the library bigger. She has helped people use the same room in a better way.

questions.correct: People speaking loudly.
questions.explanation: 第一段说明别人说话大声时，她容易找不到读到的位置。
questions.evidence: she often loses her place when people speak loudly

questions.correct: On a table near the window.
questions.explanation: 第二段明确蓝卡放在靠窗的一张桌子上。
questions.evidence: one table near the window

questions.correct: Return it before leaving.
wrong: Write a game score on it.
Give it only to Mr Lee.
questions.explanation: 借用的书签要在离开前归还。
questions.evidence: return it before leaving

questions.stem: What does the boy think of the quiet table?
questions.correct: It helps him read the story.
wrong: It is only for older students.
questions.explanation: 男孩说在这里能更好地理解故事，说明安静桌帮助了阅读。
questions.evidence: I can understand it better here

questions.stem: What is the story mainly about?
questions.correct: Making better use of a small library.
questions.explanation: 结尾点明没有扩大图书馆，而是改善同一空间的使用方式。
questions.evidence: use the same room in a better way

reading.title: The Rainy-Day Delivery
reading.text:
Ben and his sister Lily want to take three books to their grandmother on Saturday. She lives near the bus station and enjoys reading at home. Before they leave, it starts to rain.

Ben puts the books in a paper bag. Lily looks at the wet street and says, "That bag may get wet." She finds a clean plastic box with a lid. The books fit inside, but the box is too large for Ben's schoolbag. They carry it together.

At the bus stop, an old man drops his ticket. Lily picks it up while Ben holds the box. They take the next bus and arrive ten minutes later than planned.

Grandmother opens the box. The books are dry. "Thank you for being careful," she says. Ben tells her about the ticket. "A little late is fine when you stop to help someone," she replies.

questions.correct: Ben and Lily’s grandmother.
questions.explanation: 第一段说明他们要把三本书送给奶奶。
questions.evidence: take three books to their grandmother

questions.correct: To keep the books dry.
questions.explanation: 纸袋可能淋湿，因此改用带盖的塑料盒保护书。
questions.evidence: That bag may get wet

questions.correct: It is too large for Ben’s schoolbag.
questions.explanation: 盒子放不进书包，兄妹便一起搬。
questions.evidence: the box is too large for Ben's schoolbag

questions.stem: What does Lily pick up at the bus stop?
questions.correct: An old man’s ticket.
questions.explanation: 第三段先写老人掉车票，再写莉莉捡起它。
questions.evidence: an old man drops his ticket. Lily picks it up

questions.stem: How does Grandmother feel about their late arrival?
questions.correct: She understands why they are late.
wrong: She refuses to read the books.
She thinks helping is a mistake.
questions.explanation: 奶奶认为为了帮助别人而稍晚到达可以接受。
questions.evidence: A little late is fine when you stop to help someone

reading.title: Names Behind the Photos
reading.text:
There are eight old photos in our classroom cupboard. They show sports days, school trips and a music show. No one knows all the people in them.

Our teacher asks each group to choose one photo and learn its story. My group chooses a picture of students beside a red bus. We first ask the school cook. She knows the girl at the front because the girl is her daughter. The cook tells us the photo was taken on a trip to a farm.

We write the date and the names we know on a card. We do not write on the photo itself. Then we put a question on the card: "Can you help us name the others?"

Two days later, a former student visits the school. He adds four names. Our card is not complete yet, but the photo is no longer just a picture of strangers.

reading.title: A Small Part in the Play
reading.text:
Tom wants to play the king in the school play. However, the teacher gives him the part of a messenger. He has only two sentences to say. Tom feels disappointed and does not practise much.

During the first rehearsal, the king waits for a letter. Tom forgets to bring it onto the stage, so the next scene cannot begin. Everyone stops. The teacher explains, "Your letter tells the king where to go. A short part can still be important."

That evening, Tom puts a paper letter beside his shoes. Every time he practises entering the room, he remembers to take it. He also helps another student learn a long speech.

On the day of the show, Tom brings the letter at exactly the right moment. The story moves smoothly. He still says only two sentences, but this time he understands why they matter.

questions.stem: Which part does Tom receive?
questions.correct: A messenger.
questions.explanation: 老师分给汤姆的是信使角色。
questions.evidence: the part of a messenger

questions.correct: Tom forgets the letter.
questions.explanation: 信件没有送上舞台，下一场无法开始。
questions.evidence: Tom forgets to bring it onto the stage

questions.stem: Where does Tom put the practice letter that evening?
questions.correct: Beside his shoes.
questions.explanation: 第三段写到他把纸信放在鞋子旁边提醒自己。
questions.evidence: a paper letter beside his shoes

questions.stem: How does Tom change?

wrong: He asks to remove the letter.
questions.explanation: 他反复练习并准时递信，说明开始认真对待角色。
questions.evidence: at exactly the right moment

questions.stem: What is the main lesson of the story?
questions.correct: A small role can make a real difference.
wrong: The longest speech is always best.
Only kings can lead a story.
questions.explanation: 老师的解释与结尾共同说明，台词少的角色也很重要。
questions.evidence: A short part can still be important

reading.title: The Map That Changed
reading.title_zh: 【AI原创练习】会变化的周末地图
reading.text:
Nora makes a walking map for her cousin, who will visit on Sunday. She marks the bakery, the river path and a little bookshop. The whole walk should take about an hour.

On Saturday, Nora checks the route herself. A sign says the river path is closed for repairs. She draws a new line through Green Street. This route is ten minutes longer, but it has a wide pavement. Near the bookshop, she notices that the shop does not open until eleven on Sundays. She moves their starting time from nine thirty to ten thirty.

When her cousin arrives, Nora gives him the revised map. Small notes explain the changes. "I thought a map only showed places," he says. Nora smiles. "This one also tells us when we can visit them."

They reach the bakery first, share a warm roll and continue along Green Street. The plan has changed, but the walk is a success.

questions.stem: Why does Nora make the map?
questions.correct: To guide her visiting cousin.
questions.explanation: 首句说明地图是为周日来访的表亲准备的。
questions.evidence: makes a walking map for her cousin

questions.stem: Why does Nora change the route?
questions.correct: The river path is closed.
questions.explanation: 她实地检查时发现河边小路因维修关闭。
questions.evidence: closed for repairs

questions.stem: How much longer is the new route?
questions.correct: Ten minutes.
questions.explanation: 第二段明确新路线多走十分钟。
questions.evidence: This route is ten minutes longer

questions.stem: Why do they start at ten thirty instead of nine thirty?
questions.correct: The bookshop opens later on Sundays.
wrong: The river path opens at ten.
questions.explanation: 书店周日十一点开门，推迟出发可配合营业时间。
questions.evidence: the shop does not open until eleven on Sundays

questions.stem: What makes Nora’s plan useful?
questions.correct: She checks real conditions and updates it.
wrong: She keeps the shortest route at any cost.
She visits only places she owns.
questions.explanation: 她实地核查路况与营业时间并修订地图，体现计划的实用性。
questions.evidence: Small notes explain the changes

reading.title: One Envelope, Two Gardens
reading.title_zh: 【AI原创练习】一封种子两座花园
reading.text:
At the spring fair, Asha receives an envelope of bean seeds. A note inside says, "Keep half and share half." She gives five seeds to her neighbour Mr Wu and plants the other five in pots on her balcony.

For the next two weeks, Asha and Mr Wu compare notes. Her pots get morning sunlight. His garden gets more afternoon sunlight. Asha waters a little every day, while Mr Wu checks the soil before watering. Neither of them says that one way is always best.

One of Asha's pots does not produce a plant. She wants to throw the soil away, but Mr Wu suggests waiting a few more days. A small green shoot finally appears on the eighteenth day.

At the next fair, Asha brings a notebook instead of a bag of beans. It contains dates, drawings and questions from both gardens. Sharing the seeds has given her someone to learn with.

questions.correct: Five.
questions.explanation: 第一段说明她送出五粒，另五粒种在自家阳台。
questions.evidence: plants the other five

questions.stem: When do Asha’s pots get sunlight?
questions.correct: In the morning.
questions.explanation: 第二段明确她的花盆接受早晨阳光。
questions.evidence: Her pots get morning sunlight

questions.stem: What does Mr Wu do before watering?
questions.correct: He checks the soil.
questions.explanation: 文中明确吴先生先检查土壤，再决定浇水。
questions.evidence: checks the soil before watering

questions.stem: When does the late shoot appear?
questions.correct: On the eighteenth day.
questions.explanation: 第三段末句给出第十八天。
questions.evidence: on the eighteenth day

questions.stem: What does Asha gain most from sharing the seeds?
questions.correct: A partner for learning.
wrong: A prize for the largest bean.
questions.explanation: 最后一句直接点明，分享种子让她有了共同学习的人。
questions.evidence: someone to learn with

reading.title: The List on the Cupboard
reading.text:
Our art club has a cupboard full of brushes and paint. At first, anyone can take things, but nobody writes down what they use. One Thursday, we plan to paint a large poster and find that there is almost no blue paint left.

We could buy new paint immediately, but our club leader suggests checking the cupboard first. We find three small blue bottles behind a box. Some brushes are also hidden under old paper. We have enough materials after all.

After cleaning, we put a list on the door. It shows each material and its amount. A student who takes a bottle changes the number on the list. We check the numbers together at the end of each meeting.

A month later, we need yellow paint. This time, the list helps us order it before it runs out. Keeping things tidy does not mean we never buy anything; it means we know what we really need.

questions.stem: What problem do the students notice on Thursday?
questions.correct: They seem to have almost no blue paint.
wrong: The art club has no members.
questions.explanation: 第一段说准备画海报时发现蓝色颜料似乎快没了。
questions.evidence: almost no blue paint left

questions.stem: Where are the three blue bottles?
questions.correct: Behind a box.
questions.explanation: 第二段明确蓝色小瓶藏在盒子后面。
questions.evidence: three small blue bottles behind a box

questions.stem: What should a student do after taking a bottle?
questions.correct: Change the number on the list.
questions.explanation: 取用者要更新清单上的数量。
questions.evidence: changes the number on the list

questions.stem: Why can the club order yellow paint in time?
questions.correct: The list shows what is running low.
wrong: The shop sends paint every day.
They no longer use blue paint.
questions.explanation: 持续记录库存帮助他们在黄色颜料用完前订购。
questions.evidence: order it before it runs out

questions.stem: What does the passage mainly show?
questions.correct: Good records help a group use materials wisely.
wrong: Buying more is the only solution.
questions.explanation: 整理与库存记录让社团清楚真正所需的材料。
questions.evidence: we know what we really need

reading.title: Finishing in a Different Way
reading.text:
Ella enters a school fun run with her friend Dan. She wants to finish the two-kilometre route without stopping. They practise twice before the event, and she feels ready.

Halfway through the run, Dan slows down. His shoelace has come loose. Ella stops with him because the path is crowded. After he ties it, they start again. Later, a younger pupil cannot find the turn towards the playground. Ella points to the sign and walks with her until a teacher takes over.

Ella finishes later than she expected. At first, she looks unhappy. Her sports teacher asks what happened, then says, "You did not follow your original plan exactly, but you kept yourself and others safe."

Ella writes two notes in her training book. The first is to check her shoes before running. The second is to leave room in a plan for other people. Next time she will still try to run without stopping, but she will not ignore someone who needs help.

questions.stem: What is Ella’s original goal?
questions.correct: To finish the route without stopping.
wrong: To train every day for a month.
questions.explanation: 第一段直接写明她想不中途停下完成路线。
questions.evidence: finish the two-kilometre route without stopping

questions.stem: Why does Dan slow down?
questions.correct: His shoelace is loose.
wrong: He wants to visit the library.
questions.explanation: 第二段说明丹的鞋带松了。
questions.evidence: His shoelace has come loose

questions.stem: How does Ella help the younger pupil?
questions.correct: She shows and walks part of the correct way.
wrong: She carries her to the finish.
She asks her to leave the event.
She gives her a new pair of shoes.
questions.explanation: 她指明标志并陪走到老师接手。
questions.evidence: walks with her until a teacher takes over

questions.stem: What does the teacher value in Ella’s actions?
questions.correct: Care for safety and other people.
wrong: Following a plan without any change.
questions.explanation: 老师称赞她保障自己和他人的安全。
questions.evidence: kept yourself and others safe

questions.stem: What does Ella learn?
questions.correct: A goal can matter while helping others still comes first.
wrong: A training plan is always useless.
questions.explanation: 结尾保留跑步目标，同时明确不忽视需要帮助的人。
questions.evidence: she will not ignore someone who needs help

reading.title: The Repair Notebook
reading.text:
When a wheel on the classroom book trolley began to shake, everyone had an opinion. Some students wanted to replace the whole trolley. Others suggested adding more tape. Sixteen-year-old volunteer Kai asked a different question: had the problem happened before?

The librarian brought out a notebook from the cupboard. It recorded repairs made during the past year. Kai found that the same wheel had been tightened three times. Each repair worked for a few days, then the shaking returned. Simply repeating the same action was unlikely to solve the problem.

With permission, the librarian asked a trained repair worker to examine it. A small metal part was worn out. After replacing that part, the worker explained how to check the wheel safely. Students were told to report problems rather than attempt repairs themselves.

Kai added a short entry to the notebook, including the date and the worker's advice. A month later, the wheel was still steady. The trolley had not needed replacing, and the old notes had helped the school ask a better question.

questions.stem: What does Kai ask first?
questions.correct: Whether the problem has happened before.
wrong: How much tape each student owns.
Who will buy a new cupboard.
Whether books should be thrown away.
questions.explanation: 第一段末句是凯的首个问题：故障以前是否出现过。
questions.evidence: had the problem happened before

questions.stem: What do the old notes reveal?
questions.correct: The same wheel has already been tightened three times.
wrong: The trolley has never been repaired.
questions.explanation: 维修本记录同一车轮此前已拧紧三次。
questions.evidence: the same wheel had been tightened three times

questions.stem: Why is repeating the earlier repair unlikely to help?
questions.correct: Its effects have repeatedly lasted only a few days.
wrong: Tape is too expensive for the school.
The trolley is used only once a year.
questions.explanation: 每次修理只维持几天，说明同样操作没有解决根本原因。
questions.evidence: Each repair worked for a few days

questions.stem: Who replaces the worn part?
questions.correct: A trained repair worker.
questions.explanation: 图书管理员请专业维修人员检查并更换部件。
questions.evidence: After replacing that part, the worker explained

questions.stem: What is the main value of the notebook?
questions.correct: Past records help people investigate a recurring problem.
wrong: It teaches children to repair all machines alone.
It proves every old trolley must be replaced.
questions.explanation: 记录帮助识别反复故障并提出更有针对性的问题。
questions.evidence: the old notes had helped the school ask a better question

reading.title: A Better Evening Display
reading.text:
The community centre planned a small lantern display for families. A student team designed bright posters and shared a photo of the entrance online. They expected the colourful decorations to be the most useful part of their publicity.

After the first evening, visitors left comments. Several praised the lanterns, but one parent said the entrance was hard to find after dark. Another visitor had not known whether there were steps. The team realised their attractive photograph did not answer these practical questions.

For the second evening, they kept the picture but added a simple map. A volunteer checked the route and marked the entrance without steps. The new notice also stated the closing time and explained that children needed an adult with them. Volunteers stood at the two corners where visitors had previously become confused.

The next set of comments mentioned fewer difficulties finding the display. The team could not prove that the notice alone caused this change; the extra volunteers may also have helped. Still, they learned that useful information should be planned as carefully as an attractive design.

questions.stem: What does the team initially expect to attract families?
questions.correct: The colourful decorations in their publicity.
questions.explanation: 第一段写团队原先重视装饰与漂亮的入口照片。
questions.evidence: the colourful decorations to be the most useful part

questions.stem: What question does a visitor have after the first evening?
questions.correct: Whether there are steps at the entrance.
wrong: Whether the lanterns are for sale.
Whether the centre has a swimming pool.
questions.explanation: 第二段直接提及访客不了解入口是否有台阶。
questions.evidence: whether there were steps

questions.stem: What does the revised notice include?
questions.correct: A map and the closing time.
questions.explanation: 新版信息既有地图，也写了闭馆时间。
questions.evidence: The new notice also stated the closing time

questions.stem: Why can’t the team credit only the new notice for the improvement?
questions.correct: Extra volunteers may have helped too.
wrong: No visitors came the second evening.
All comments were written before the changes.
questions.explanation: 团队同时增加志愿者，不能把变化只归因于公告。
questions.evidence: the extra volunteers may also have helped

questions.stem: What does the team learn about publicity?
questions.correct: Practical information deserves as much care as appearance.
wrong: A beautiful picture answers every question.
Visitor comments should always be ignored.
questions.explanation: 结尾强调实用信息应与吸引人的设计一样认真规划。
questions.evidence: useful information should be planned as carefully as an attractive design

reading.title: Choosing Books for the Corner
reading.text:
The school gave Class Eight enough money for twelve new books. Each student suggested a favourite title. At first, the class planned to buy the twelve titles with the most votes. Then their teacher asked them to look at who had voted.

Almost all the suggestions came from students who already used the reading corner. Several quieter classmates had not written anything. When the book team spoke with them, they discovered that some wanted short books with clear pictures, while others hoped for books about practical skills.

The team did not cancel the vote. Instead, they reserved four places for needs that the first list had missed. They also borrowed sample copies before placing the order. One popular book turned out to have print that was too small for comfortable reading, so they chose another edition of the same story.

After a month, different students were borrowing the new books. The team kept a suggestion sheet beside the shelves. They had learned that listening to the loudest group was a starting point, rather than a complete picture of what the class needed.

questions.stem: How many new books can the class buy?
questions.correct: Twelve.
questions.explanation: 首句写明经费足够购买十二本书。
questions.evidence: twelve new books

questions.stem: Who supplied most of the first suggestions?
questions.correct: Students already using the reading corner.
questions.explanation: 第二段说明最初建议主要来自原本就在使用阅读角的学生。
questions.evidence: students who already used the reading corner

questions.stem: What does the team do with four places on the list?
questions.correct: Reserve them for overlooked needs.
wrong: Remove them to save all the money.
questions.explanation: 团队预留四个名额满足初始清单遗漏的需求。
questions.evidence: reserved four places for needs that the first list had missed

questions.stem: Why does the team change the edition of one story?
questions.correct: The original edition has uncomfortable small print.
questions.explanation: 样书试读发现字号太小，所以更换同一故事的版本。
questions.evidence: print that was too small for comfortable reading

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
questions.correct: Considering less-heard needs when making a group choice.
wrong: Making every student read the same story.
questions.explanation: 结尾强调最积极群体的意见不能代表全班所有需求。
questions.evidence: rather than a complete picture of what the class needed

reading.title: The Noise Diary
reading.text:
Residents near Elm Square disagreed about the noise from evening activities. Some blamed the basketball court, while others thought most noise came from delivery vehicles. The neighbourhood youth group offered to keep a diary instead of guessing.

For one week, volunteers stood at two agreed places between six and eight each evening. They noted the time, the kind of sound and whether it interrupted a short conversation. They did not record people's voices or photograph individuals. Their purpose was to describe a shared problem, not identify people to blame.

The diary showed that a brief period of vehicle unloading often overlapped with the final basketball game. On rainy evenings, both activities were less frequent. The volunteers were careful not to call their notes precise scientific measurements; different people might judge the same sound differently.

At a meeting, residents agreed to try moving unloading fifteen minutes earlier and reminding players of the closing time. They planned another week of notes after the changes. The diary had not settled every disagreement, but it had given neighbours specific times and situations to discuss.

questions.stem: Why does the youth group keep a diary?
questions.correct: To replace guesses with observations.
wrong: To choose a new name for the square.
questions.explanation: 首段指出大家对来源有争议，青年组提议记录而非猜测。
questions.evidence: keep a diary instead of guessing

questions.stem: What do the volunteers avoid doing?
questions.correct: Recording people’s voices.
questions.explanation: 第二段明确不录人声、不拍摄个人。
questions.evidence: They did not record people's voices

questions.stem: What often happens at the same time?
questions.correct: Vehicle unloading and the final basketball game.
wrong: A concert and a swimming lesson.
A school exam and a delivery break.
questions.explanation: 第三段记载卸货与最后一场篮球活动常有重叠。
questions.evidence: vehicle unloading often overlapped with the final basketball game

questions.stem: Why do volunteers avoid calling the diary precise scientific measurements?
questions.correct: People can judge the same sound differently.
wrong: They forget to write any times.
They work only on one sunny morning.
They measure every sound with identical equipment.
questions.explanation: 原文明确人的主观判断存在差异。
questions.evidence: different people might judge the same sound differently

questions.stem: Why is another week of notes planned?
questions.correct: To observe what happens after the changes.
wrong: To prove the players are always wrong.
To replace all evening activities with silence.
questions.explanation: 先调整时间，再记录一周，是为了观察调整后的情况。
questions.evidence: another week of notes after the changes

reading.title: More Than a Short Label
reading.title_zh: 【AI原创练习】展品标签不只是短句
reading.text:
For a local history exhibition, students wrote labels for everyday objects donated by residents. Lina's group received a metal lunch box. Their first label described its colour, size and age. It was accurate, but visitors usually walked past without stopping.

The group returned to the woman who had donated it. She explained that her father had carried the box to work, then used it to store letters after retiring. A dent in the lid came from a fall during a bus journey, not from factory work as the students had guessed.

With the woman's permission, they added two sentences about those memories. They kept the basic description and clearly marked the memories as her account. They did not present every detail as something proved by the object itself.

More visitors paused at the display, and one asked how families decide which ordinary things to keep. Lina realised that a good label could help people ask questions. It did not need to turn a lunch box into a treasure or hide the limits of what was known.

questions.stem: What does the first label mainly describe?
questions.correct: The box’s physical features and age.
wrong: The price of a new lunch box.
questions.explanation: 第一段列出初版标签写了颜色、大小和年代。
questions.evidence: its colour, size and age

questions.stem: What caused the dent in the lid?
questions.correct: A fall during a bus journey.

reading.title: A Calendar with Blank Spaces
reading.text:
When Leo joined the school guitar group, he filled every evening of his calendar with an hour of practice. He thought a serious learner should never leave a blank space. During the first week, however, homework and a family visit meant he missed two evenings. He felt the whole plan had failed.

His music teacher asked him to describe what happened during the evenings he did practise. Leo admitted that he often played the easy opening repeatedly and avoided a difficult change between two chords. The number of minutes alone did not show what he was learning.

They made a smaller plan: fifteen focused minutes on the difficult change, followed by a song he enjoyed. Two evenings were left unplanned so he could move a session when necessary. In his notebook, he wrote what had become easier and what still needed attention.

After three weeks, Leo could make the change more smoothly. He did not conclude that short practice was always better for everyone. He had found a plan that matched his present needs and was easier to keep.

reading.title: When the Headline Was Wrong
reading.text:
The student newspaper published a headline saying that the school would remove all paper notices. It was based on a short interview about a trial digital noticeboard in one corridor. By lunchtime, several students were asking how clubs without regular computer access would advertise events.

Editor Mei checked the interview notes. The speaker had described a limited trial, not a decision covering the whole school. Mei could have quietly changed the online headline. Instead, she discussed a visible correction with the team. They replaced the headline, added a note explaining the error, and linked to a fuller description of the trial.

Some readers thanked them; others said the mistake had already caused confusion. Mei accepted that a correction could not erase the original effect. The team also changed its routine. Future headlines about policy would be checked against the source notes by a second editor before publication.

A month later, another report mentioned a proposal rather than an approved decision. This time the headline preserved that distinction. The newspaper had not become incapable of making mistakes, but it had made both its correction process and its checking process more visible.

reading.title: Testing the Route Together
reading.text:
A youth committee designed a route from the bus stop to a new community reading room. On the map, the shortest path looked obvious: cross the square and use the side entrance. Committee members initially called it the easiest route.

Before printing the map, they invited residents with different needs to test it. A wheelchair user found that a low step blocked the side entrance. A parent pushing a buggy found the turn beside a planter too narrow. An older resident said the small arrows were difficult to see. These were not problems the committee had noticed during its first walk.

The building manager confirmed that the main entrance had a step-free approach. The group revised the route, which added about two minutes, and used larger, higher-contrast arrows. They also described the surface and entrances in words, so visitors could decide which route suited them.

The revised map did not claim to remove every possible barrier. A contact number invited reports of new difficulties. The committee had learned that calling a route easy required more than timing a walk by people whose needs were alike.

reading.title: What the Percentage Hid
reading.text:
At a student council meeting, two clubs reported their survey results. The film club said that eighty percent of its respondents wanted a Friday screening. The science club reported sixty percent support for a Saturday workshop. Some members immediately argued that the film event had wider support.

Jules asked to see the numbers behind the percentages. The film club had received twenty responses, so sixteen people supported its proposal. The science club had received forty responses, of whom twenty-four supported the workshop. Neither survey included every student, and each club had mainly asked its own members.

This did not prove that the science event was more popular across the school. It showed that the percentages answered a narrower question: what share of each responding group supported that group's proposal? The groups differed in size and were not selected to represent the whole school.

The council decided to send both proposals through the same school-wide channel, with one response allowed per student and a clear closing date. Jules still used percentages in the final report, but placed the counts beside them. A neat number, he had learned, needs enough context to be understood.

reading.title: Opening the Recommendation Window
reading.text:
At the start of a reading project, Hana used an app that suggested articles similar to ones she had opened before. After she read several pieces about mountain travel, the suggestions filled with hiking routes and equipment reviews. She enjoyed them, but began to assume that this was what most people were discussing.

During a class exchange, other students brought articles about local theatre, public transport and food traditions. Hana realised that her personal list was a window shaped partly by her own earlier choices. It was not a neutral picture of everything being published.

She did not delete the app. Instead, she kept its recommendations for quick browsing and added a weekly visit to a general library page. She also chose one topic suggested by a classmate and read beyond the first headline. In her project diary, she recorded where each article had come from.

The new habit sometimes led to articles she did not enjoy, and it took more effort than simply following the next suggestion. Yet it helped her separate "often shown to me" from "important to everyone." Useful recommendations could remain useful without becoming her only way of discovering ideas.

reading.title: A Trial in the Courtyard
reading.text:
Students at Brook School wanted more comfortable places to read outdoors. The facilities team agreed to test a movable shade above one courtyard bench for two weeks. A student group planned to compare how often that bench was used before and during the trial.

Their first chart looked impressive: afternoon use rose from six recorded visits in the earlier week to eighteen in the trial week. However, Mara noticed that the earlier week had included three rainy afternoons, while the trial week was dry. A reading club had also begun meeting in the courtyard. These differences made a simple before-and-after claim less convincing.

The group revised its report. They described the increase but did not attribute all of it to the shade. They also asked users about comfort, noted weather conditions and observed another bench nearby. The evidence still had limits: two benches could differ in location, and a short trial could not represent every season.

The team recommended keeping the movable shade for further testing rather than immediately ordering one for every outdoor space. Their report sounded less dramatic than the first chart, but it gave the school a clearer basis for its next decision.

reading.title: The Missing Half of Reuse
reading.title_zh: 【AI原创练习】重复使用的另一半
reading.text:
A youth centre introduced reusable cups for its weekend events. Organisers expected the change to reduce the number of disposable cups bought each month. In the first three weekends, however, many reusable cups disappeared from the return area, and volunteers repeatedly had to search meeting rooms for them.

Instead of assuming visitors did not care, the team followed the cups' journey. The drinks table was beside the entrance, but the only return box stood behind a door near the kitchen. Some guests thought they should leave empty cups on tables for staff. Others could not find the box before their bus arrived.

The centre placed clearly marked return boxes beside both exits and explained the return process when serving drinks. It also arranged enough time and staff for washing between sessions. A reusable item was useful only if the system made repeated use practical.

By the following month, more cups were being returned and fewer replacements were needed. The team continued tracking losses and cleaning needs rather than claiming the change had no costs. The project taught them to design the return journey with as much care as the moment when an item was first handed out.

listening.title: Returning Library Books

listening.title: Feedback on the Walking Tour

listening.transcript_zh: 感谢试走学生导览路线。本次希望收集路线反馈，而非导游音量评价。请填写出口附近的短表。第一题问哪个标志最难看懂，第二题问在哪里想休息。姓名可以不填。我们会比较反馈后再调整下月路线。若发现紧急安全问题，请现在告知工作人员，不要等表格被阅读后才处理。

questions.explanation: 紧急问题应立即告知工作人员。

listening.title: Recording the School Story
listening.title_zh: 【AI原创·设备朗读】录制校园故事
listening.text: The history club will record a short school story on Wednesday. We originally booked the music room, but a rehearsal is now taking place there. listening.transcript_zh: 历史社周三录制校园短故事。原订音乐教室当天有排练，改用办公室旁的小会议室。请三点四十五分到场试音，四点开始录制。带上最新修改后的定稿。涉及真人姓名时应先征得同意，也可删去姓名而保留故事主线。成品经社团老师检查后再上传。

questions.stem: Why has the recording room changed?

The music room must be repainted.

listening.title: How the Puzzle Swap Works
listening.title_zh: 【AI原创·设备朗读】拼图交换规则
listening.text: At Saturday's puzzle swap, volunteers will check that each puzzle has all its pieces before giving out a swap token. listening.transcript_zh: 周六拼图交换活动中，志愿者确认拼图片数完整后才发交换券。每张券可换一份检查过的拼图，不按盒子大小区分。缺片拼图放在另设的手工材料箱，不换券。活动十点到十二点，最后收件时间十一点半，以便检查。也欢迎不带物品、只来参观的人。

questions.stem: When is a swap token given?
questions.correct: After a puzzle is checked for completeness.
wrong: Whenever someone brings any empty box.
questions.explanation: 确认完整后发券。

listening.title: Notes for the Outdoor Lesson
listening.title_zh: 【AI原创·设备朗读】户外课观察记录
listening.text: For tomorrow's outdoor lesson, each group will compare two places in the playground. Choose one open area and one area beside a wall. We can discuss what we have already observed instead of finishing every box outside.
listening.transcript_zh: 明天户外课每组比较操场两处：一处开阔地和一处墙边。记录时间，描述两处空气给人的感受。这是观察练习，没有温度计就不要编造温度。尽量使用一致的词描述两处。若下大雨，应随老师回教室，可以讨论已有观察，无须坚持在外面填满所有格子。

questions.stem: Which two places should each group compare?

wrong: A bus stop and a shop.

questions.evidence: one open area and one area beside a wall

questions.explanation: 没有仪器不能虚构精确温度。
questions.evidence: do not invent temperatures

questions.correct: Return with the teacher and discuss existing observations.
wrong: Stay outside until every box is filled.
Change every observation to a guessed number.
questions.explanation: 大雨时返回教室，再讨论已经观察到的情况。
questions.evidence: return to the classroom with your teacher

listening.title: Signing Up for the Drama Project
listening.title_zh: 【AI原创·设备朗读】戏剧项目报名
listening.text: Our drama project needs people for acting, sound and making props. You do not have to act to join. listening.title: Preparing a Family Audio Story
listening.title_zh: 【AI原创·设备朗读】准备家庭音频故事
listening.text: For our English project, you may record a family member describing a favourite place. The story should be between one and two minutes long. If recording at home is difficult, book a school room with me on Friday.

listening.title: Interpreting the Trial Results
listening.title_zh: 【AI原创·设备朗读】理解试点结果
listening.text: Our homework-planner trial has finished its first week. Eighteen of the thirty students who returned a feedback form said the planner helped them remember deadlines. That is encouraging, but it does not tell us what all students think. Some students tried the planner without returning a form, and others did not use it at all. In next week's report, please give the number of responses as well as the percentage. We will invite feedback from non-users too, especially about reasons they did not try it. The aim is to improve the tool, not to make the first results sound more impressive than they are.
listening.transcript_zh: 作业计划工具第一周试点结束。交反馈表的三十名学生中，十八名认为工具帮助记住截止时间。这是积极信号，但不能代表所有学生：有人使用却没交表，也有人未使用。下周报告请同时写答卷人数和百分比，并向未使用者了解原因。目标是改进工具，而非夸大首轮结果。

questions.correct: Reasons they did not try the planner.

questions.evidence: reasons they did not try it

listening.title: Checking a Photo Caption
listening.title_zh: 【AI原创·设备朗读】核对照片说明
listening.text: Before we publish the archive photo, we need to correct its caption. The original note says the picture shows the opening of the town pool in nineteen eighty-four. However, the banner in the photograph names a school sports event, and a second record gives a different date. We have confirmed the location, but not the year. For now, describe it as a school event at the town pool, with the date still being checked. Please keep the old note in our records rather than deleting it. questions.stem: How should the event be described for now?

wrong: The pool’s opening in a confirmed year.
An event with no possible connection to a school.
questions.explanation: 临时说明需保留已知活动性质与地点，并说明日期未定。
questions.evidence: with the date still being checked

questions.stem: Why should the old note be kept?
questions.correct: To document the earlier description and the reason for changing it.
wrong: To prove its date must be right.
questions.explanation: 旧记录有助追溯说法形成及更正原因。

listening.title: Choosing a Shuttle Timetable
listening.title_zh: 【AI原创·设备朗读】选择接驳车时刻
listening.text: The community centre is considering two shuttle timetables. The first would bring visitors just before the morning classes. The second would arrive twenty minutes earlier, leaving more waiting time but allowing passengers to visit the reception desk before lessons. We are not asking which timetable has the shorter journey; the journey itself is the same. Please choose the arrival time that better suits your needs and explain why. People who do not currently use the shuttle may also respond. Their answers may reveal barriers that a survey of existing passengers alone would miss. No timetable change will take effect until a final notice is issued.
listening.transcript_zh: 社区中心正在比较两种接驳车时刻：一种在上午课程开始前不久到达，另一种提前二十分钟到，等待更久，但可先去服务台。两种方案车程相同，调查不是比较行车时间。请选更适合的到达时刻并说明原因。未使用接驳车者也可答，以了解现有乘客调查可能遗漏的障碍。最终通知发出前不会改时刻。

listening.title: Reviewing the Welcome Guide

listening.text: Our volunteer team has drafted an English welcome guide for the community centre. Before it is printed, please check the practical details against the current noticeboard. A staff member will resolve those points. We will then ask two new visitors to follow the guide and tell us where they become confused.
listening.transcript_zh: 志愿者团队已写好社区中心英文欢迎指南。印刷前请对照当前公告板核实实用信息。周末开放时间上月调整过，旧传单的房间名称也不可靠。英语流畅很重要，但时间错了仍会让访客吃闭门羹。无法确认的信息先标记，不要猜，由工作人员核实。之后请两位新访客按指南试走，指出困惑。

questions.stem: What should reviewers use to check details?
questions.correct: The current noticeboard.
questions.explanation: 要求对照当前公告板核实。
questions.evidence: against the current noticeboard

questions.stem: What point does the closed-door example illustrate?
questions.correct: Accurate details matter as well as good language.
wrong: Longer sentences are always more helpful.
questions.explanation: 句子再优美，错误时间也会误导访客，强调语言与事实都要准确。

listening.title: Evaluating the Borrowing Baskets
listening.title_zh: 【AI原创·设备朗读】评估借用篮子
listening.text: Our market tested borrowing baskets for two weekends. Volunteers counted forty returns on the first weekend and fifty on the second. Those figures alone do not show that the return rate improved, because more baskets were also borrowed on the second weekend. Please compare returns with the number borrowed in each period. We should also keep records of baskets that were returned late, since a basket missing on Sunday may arrive on Monday. The next report will separate same-day returns from later returns. This will help us plan how many baskets must be available without treating every delayed return as a permanent loss.
listening.transcript_zh: 市场借篮试点进行了两个周末，回收数分别四十和五十。第二周末借出数量也更多，因此单凭回收数量不能断言归还率提高。应比较各期归还数与借出数，也要记录晚还的篮子：周日没回来的可能周一归还。下份报告区分当日归还与迟还，以便安排库存，避免把迟还全算作永久丢失。

questions.stem: How many baskets are returned on the second weekend?

wrong: Every basket was lost on Monday.
No baskets were borrowed the first weekend.
The market refuses all late returns.

questions.stem: What will the next report distinguish?

listening.title: Writing Fair Discussion Notes
listening.title_zh: 【AI原创·设备朗读】记录公平的讨论纪要
listening.text: When writing notes from our student discussion, please separate decisions from suggestions. Several people supported opening the study room on Saturday, but the group has not yet agreed on staffing. It is therefore a proposal, not an approved arrangement. Include the main concern about supervision as well as the reasons in favour. You do not need to name each speaker; group the points by topic. This review is intended to check whether their points were represented accurately, not to remove every opinion that someone disagrees with.

reading_sets.title: A Table for Quiet Reading
reading_sets.passage:
Our school library is small. After lunch, some students read there, but others talk about their games. Mia likes reading stories, yet she often loses her place when people speak loudly.

On Monday, she tells Mr Lee about the problem. He does not ask everyone to leave. Instead, he puts a blue card on one table near the window. The card says, "Quiet reading here." Students can still talk softly at the other tables.

Mia makes a small box for bookmarks. Anyone at the blue-card table can borrow one and return it before leaving. On Friday, six students sit at the table. One boy is reading his first story in English. "I can understand it better here," he says.

Mia is happy. She has not made the library bigger. She has helped people use the same room in a better way.

reading_sets.title: The Rainy-Day Delivery
reading_sets.passage:
Ben and his sister Lily want to take three books to their grandmother on Saturday. She lives near the bus station and enjoys reading at home. Before they leave, it starts to rain.

Ben puts the books in a paper bag. Lily looks at the wet street and says, "That bag may get wet." She finds a clean plastic box with a lid. The books fit inside, but the box is too large for Ben's schoolbag. They carry it together.

At the bus stop, an old man drops his ticket. Lily picks it up while Ben holds the box. They take the next bus and arrive ten minutes later than planned.

Grandmother opens the box. The books are dry. "Thank you for being careful," she says. Ben tells her about the ticket. "A little late is fine when you stop to help someone," she replies.

reading_sets.title: Names Behind the Photos
reading_sets.passage:
There are eight old photos in our classroom cupboard. They show sports days, school trips and a music show. No one knows all the people in them.

Our teacher asks each group to choose one photo and learn its story. My group chooses a picture of students beside a red bus. We first ask the school cook. She knows the girl at the front because the girl is her daughter. The cook tells us the photo was taken on a trip to a farm.

We write the date and the names we know on a card. We do not write on the photo itself. Then we put a question on the card: "Can you help us name the others?"

Two days later, a former student visits the school. He adds four names. Our card is not complete yet, but the photo is no longer just a picture of strangers.

reading_sets.title: A Small Part in the Play
reading_sets.passage:
Tom wants to play the king in the school play. However, the teacher gives him the part of a messenger. He has only two sentences to say. Tom feels disappointed and does not practise much.

During the first rehearsal, the king waits for a letter. Tom forgets to bring it onto the stage, so the next scene cannot begin. Everyone stops. The teacher explains, "Your letter tells the king where to go. A short part can still be important."

That evening, Tom puts a paper letter beside his shoes. Every time he practises entering the room, he remembers to take it. He also helps another student learn a long speech.

On the day of the show, Tom brings the letter at exactly the right moment. The story moves smoothly. He still says only two sentences, but this time he understands why they matter.

reading_sets.title: The Map That Changed
reading_sets.title_zh: 【AI原创练习】会变化的周末地图
reading_sets.passage:
Nora makes a walking map for her cousin, who will visit on Sunday. She marks the bakery, the river path and a little bookshop. The whole walk should take about an hour.

On Saturday, Nora checks the route herself. A sign says the river path is closed for repairs. She draws a new line through Green Street. This route is ten minutes longer, but it has a wide pavement. Near the bookshop, she notices that the shop does not open until eleven on Sundays. She moves their starting time from nine thirty to ten thirty.

When her cousin arrives, Nora gives him the revised map. Small notes explain the changes. "I thought a map only showed places," he says. Nora smiles. "This one also tells us when we can visit them."

They reach the bakery first, share a warm roll and continue along Green Street. The plan has changed, but the walk is a success.

reading_sets.title: One Envelope, Two Gardens
reading_sets.title_zh: 【AI原创练习】一封种子两座花园
reading_sets.passage:
At the spring fair, Asha receives an envelope of bean seeds. A note inside says, "Keep half and share half." She gives five seeds to her neighbour Mr Wu and plants the other five in pots on her balcony.

For the next two weeks, Asha and Mr Wu compare notes. Her pots get morning sunlight. His garden gets more afternoon sunlight. Asha waters a little every day, while Mr Wu checks the soil before watering. Neither of them says that one way is always best.

One of Asha's pots does not produce a plant. She wants to throw the soil away, but Mr Wu suggests waiting a few more days. A small green shoot finally appears on the eighteenth day.

At the next fair, Asha brings a notebook instead of a bag of beans. It contains dates, drawings and questions from both gardens. Sharing the seeds has given her someone to learn with.

reading_sets.title: The List on the Cupboard
reading_sets.passage:
Our art club has a cupboard full of brushes and paint. At first, anyone can take things, but nobody writes down what they use. One Thursday, we plan to paint a large poster and find that there is almost no blue paint left.

We could buy new paint immediately, but our club leader suggests checking the cupboard first. We find three small blue bottles behind a box. Some brushes are also hidden under old paper. We have enough materials after all.

After cleaning, we put a list on the door. It shows each material and its amount. A student who takes a bottle changes the number on the list. We check the numbers together at the end of each meeting.

A month later, we need yellow paint. This time, the list helps us order it before it runs out. Keeping things tidy does not mean we never buy anything; it means we know what we really need.

reading_sets.title: Finishing in a Different Way
reading_sets.passage:
Ella enters a school fun run with her friend Dan. She wants to finish the two-kilometre route without stopping. They practise twice before the event, and she feels ready.

Halfway through the run, Dan slows down. His shoelace has come loose. Ella stops with him because the path is crowded. After he ties it, they start again. Later, a younger pupil cannot find the turn towards the playground. Ella points to the sign and walks with her until a teacher takes over.

Ella finishes later than she expected. At first, she looks unhappy. Her sports teacher asks what happened, then says, "You did not follow your original plan exactly, but you kept yourself and others safe."

Ella writes two notes in her training book. The first is to check her shoes before running. The second is to leave room in a plan for other people. Next time she will still try to run without stopping, but she will not ignore someone who needs help.

reading_sets.title: The Repair Notebook
reading_sets.passage:
When a wheel on the classroom book trolley began to shake, everyone had an opinion. Some students wanted to replace the whole trolley. Others suggested adding more tape. Sixteen-year-old volunteer Kai asked a different question: had the problem happened before?

The librarian brought out a notebook from the cupboard. It recorded repairs made during the past year. Kai found that the same wheel had been tightened three times. Each repair worked for a few days, then the shaking returned. Simply repeating the same action was unlikely to solve the problem.

With permission, the librarian asked a trained repair worker to examine it. A small metal part was worn out. After replacing that part, the worker explained how to check the wheel safely. Students were told to report problems rather than attempt repairs themselves.

Kai added a short entry to the notebook, including the date and the worker's advice. A month later, the wheel was still steady. The trolley had not needed replacing, and the old notes had helped the school ask a better question.

reading_sets.title: A Better Evening Display
reading_sets.passage:
The community centre planned a small lantern display for families. A student team designed bright posters and shared a photo of the entrance online. They expected the colourful decorations to be the most useful part of their publicity.

After the first evening, visitors left comments. Several praised the lanterns, but one parent said the entrance was hard to find after dark. Another visitor had not known whether there were steps. The team realised their attractive photograph did not answer these practical questions.

For the second evening, they kept the picture but added a simple map. A volunteer checked the route and marked the entrance without steps. The new notice also stated the closing time and explained that children needed an adult with them. Volunteers stood at the two corners where visitors had previously become confused.

The next set of comments mentioned fewer difficulties finding the display. The team could not prove that the notice alone caused this change; the extra volunteers may also have helped. Still, they learned that useful information should be planned as carefully as an attractive design.

reading_sets.title: Choosing Books for the Corner
reading_sets.passage:
The school gave Class Eight enough money for twelve new books. Each student suggested a favourite title. At first, the class planned to buy the twelve titles with the most votes. Then their teacher asked them to look at who had voted.

Almost all the suggestions came from students who already used the reading corner. Several quieter classmates had not written anything. When the book team spoke with them, they discovered that some wanted short books with clear pictures, while others hoped for books about practical skills.

The team did not cancel the vote. Instead, they reserved four places for needs that the first list had missed. They also borrowed sample copies before placing the order. One popular book turned out to have print that was too small for comfortable reading, so they chose another edition of the same story.

After a month, different students were borrowing the new books. The team kept a suggestion sheet beside the shelves. They had learned that listening to the loudest group was a starting point, rather than a complete picture of what the class needed.

reading_sets.title: The Noise Diary
reading_sets.passage:
Residents near Elm Square disagreed about the noise from evening activities. Some blamed the basketball court, while others thought most noise came from delivery vehicles. The neighbourhood youth group offered to keep a diary instead of guessing.

For one week, volunteers stood at two agreed places between six and eight each evening. They noted the time, the kind of sound and whether it interrupted a short conversation. They did not record people's voices or photograph individuals. Their purpose was to describe a shared problem, not identify people to blame.

The diary showed that a brief period of vehicle unloading often overlapped with the final basketball game. On rainy evenings, both activities were less frequent. The volunteers were careful not to call their notes precise scientific measurements; different people might judge the same sound differently.

At a meeting, residents agreed to try moving unloading fifteen minutes earlier and reminding players of the closing time. They planned another week of notes after the changes. The diary had not settled every disagreement, but it had given neighbours specific times and situations to discuss.

reading_sets.title: More Than a Short Label
reading_sets.title_zh: 【AI原创练习】展品标签不只是短句
reading_sets.passage:
For a local history exhibition, students wrote labels for everyday objects donated by residents. Lina's group received a metal lunch box. Their first label described its colour, size and age. It was accurate, but visitors usually walked past without stopping.

The group returned to the woman who had donated it. She explained that her father had carried the box to work, then used it to store letters after retiring. A dent in the lid came from a fall during a bus journey, not from factory work as the students had guessed.

With the woman's permission, they added two sentences about those memories. They kept the basic description and clearly marked the memories as her account. They did not present every detail as something proved by the object itself.

More visitors paused at the display, and one asked how families decide which ordinary things to keep. Lina realised that a good label could help people ask questions. It did not need to turn a lunch box into a treasure or hide the limits of what was known.

reading_sets.title: A Calendar with Blank Spaces
reading_sets.passage:
When Leo joined the school guitar group, he filled every evening of his calendar with an hour of practice. He thought a serious learner should never leave a blank space. During the first week, however, homework and a family visit meant he missed two evenings. He felt the whole plan had failed.

His music teacher asked him to describe what happened during the evenings he did practise. Leo admitted that he often played the easy opening repeatedly and avoided a difficult change between two chords. The number of minutes alone did not show what he was learning.

They made a smaller plan: fifteen focused minutes on the difficult change, followed by a song he enjoyed. Two evenings were left unplanned so he could move a session when necessary. In his notebook, he wrote what had become easier and what still needed attention.

After three weeks, Leo could make the change more smoothly. He did not conclude that short practice was always better for everyone. He had found a plan that matched his present needs and was easier to keep.

reading_sets.title: When the Headline Was Wrong
reading_sets.passage:
The student newspaper published a headline saying that the school would remove all paper notices. It was based on a short interview about a trial digital noticeboard in one corridor. By lunchtime, several students were asking how clubs without regular computer access would advertise events.

Editor Mei checked the interview notes. The speaker had described a limited trial, not a decision covering the whole school. Mei could have quietly changed the online headline. Instead, she discussed a visible correction with the team. They replaced the headline, added a note explaining the error, and linked to a fuller description of the trial.

Some readers thanked them; others said the mistake had already caused confusion. Mei accepted that a correction could not erase the original effect. The team also changed its routine. Future headlines about policy would be checked against the source notes by a second editor before publication.

A month later, another report mentioned a proposal rather than an approved decision. This time the headline preserved that distinction. The newspaper had not become incapable of making mistakes, but it had made both its correction process and its checking process more visible.

reading_sets.title: Testing the Route Together
reading_sets.passage:
A youth committee designed a route from the bus stop to a new community reading room. On the map, the shortest path looked obvious: cross the square and use the side entrance. Committee members initially called it the easiest route.

Before printing the map, they invited residents with different needs to test it. A wheelchair user found that a low step blocked the side entrance. A parent pushing a buggy found the turn beside a planter too narrow. An older resident said the small arrows were difficult to see. These were not problems the committee had noticed during its first walk.

The building manager confirmed that the main entrance had a step-free approach. The group revised the route, which added about two minutes, and used larger, higher-contrast arrows. They also described the surface and entrances in words, so visitors could decide which route suited them.

The revised map did not claim to remove every possible barrier. A contact number invited reports of new difficulties. The committee had learned that calling a route easy required more than timing a walk by people whose needs were alike.

reading_sets.title: What the Percentage Hid
reading_sets.passage:
At a student council meeting, two clubs reported their survey results. The film club said that eighty percent of its respondents wanted a Friday screening. The science club reported sixty percent support for a Saturday workshop. Some members immediately argued that the film event had wider support.

Jules asked to see the numbers behind the percentages. The film club had received twenty responses, so sixteen people supported its proposal. The science club had received forty responses, of whom twenty-four supported the workshop. Neither survey included every student, and each club had mainly asked its own members.

This did not prove that the science event was more popular across the school. It showed that the percentages answered a narrower question: what share of each responding group supported that group's proposal? The groups differed in size and were not selected to represent the whole school.

The council decided to send both proposals through the same school-wide channel, with one response allowed per student and a clear closing date. Jules still used percentages in the final report, but placed the counts beside them. A neat number, he had learned, needs enough context to be understood.

reading_sets.title: Opening the Recommendation Window
reading_sets.passage:
At the start of a reading project, Hana used an app that suggested articles similar to ones she had opened before. After she read several pieces about mountain travel, the suggestions filled with hiking routes and equipment reviews. She enjoyed them, but began to assume that this was what most people were discussing.

During a class exchange, other students brought articles about local theatre, public transport and food traditions. Hana realised that her personal list was a window shaped partly by her own earlier choices. It was not a neutral picture of everything being published.

She did not delete the app. Instead, she kept its recommendations for quick browsing and added a weekly visit to a general library page. She also chose one topic suggested by a classmate and read beyond the first headline. In her project diary, she recorded where each article had come from.

The new habit sometimes led to articles she did not enjoy, and it took more effort than simply following the next suggestion. Yet it helped her separate "often shown to me" from "important to everyone." Useful recommendations could remain useful without becoming her only way of discovering ideas.

reading_sets.title: A Trial in the Courtyard
reading_sets.passage:
Students at Brook School wanted more comfortable places to read outdoors. The facilities team agreed to test a movable shade above one courtyard bench for two weeks. A student group planned to compare how often that bench was used before and during the trial.

Their first chart looked impressive: afternoon use rose from six recorded visits in the earlier week to eighteen in the trial week. However, Mara noticed that the earlier week had included three rainy afternoons, while the trial week was dry. A reading club had also begun meeting in the courtyard. These differences made a simple before-and-after claim less convincing.

The group revised its report. They described the increase but did not attribute all of it to the shade. They also asked users about comfort, noted weather conditions and observed another bench nearby. The evidence still had limits: two benches could differ in location, and a short trial could not represent every season.

The team recommended keeping the movable shade for further testing rather than immediately ordering one for every outdoor space. Their report sounded less dramatic than the first chart, but it gave the school a clearer basis for its next decision.

reading_sets.title: The Missing Half of Reuse
reading_sets.title_zh: 【AI原创练习】重复使用的另一半
reading_sets.passage:
A youth centre introduced reusable cups for its weekend events. Organisers expected the change to reduce the number of disposable cups bought each month. In the first three weekends, however, many reusable cups disappeared from the return area, and volunteers repeatedly had to search meeting rooms for them.

Instead of assuming visitors did not care, the team followed the cups' journey. The drinks table was beside the entrance, but the only return box stood behind a door near the kitchen. Some guests thought they should leave empty cups on tables for staff. Others could not find the box before their bus arrived.

The centre placed clearly marked return boxes beside both exits and explained the return process when serving drinks. It also arranged enough time and staff for washing between sessions. A reusable item was useful only if the system made repeated use practical.

By the following month, more cups were being returned and fewer replacements were needed. The team continued tracking losses and cleaning needs rather than claiming the change had no costs. The project taught them to design the return journey with as much care as the moment when an item was first handed out.

reading_questions.explanation: 图书管理员请专业维修人员检查并更换部件。 原文依据：After replacing that part, the worker explained

reading_questions.stem: What is the main value of the notebook?
reading_questions.explanation: 记录帮助识别反复故障并提出更有针对性的问题。 原文依据：the old notes had helped the school ask a better question

reading_questions.stem: What does the team initially expect to attract families?
reading_questions.explanation: 第一段写团队原先重视装饰与漂亮的入口照片。 原文依据：the colourful decorations to be the most useful part

reading_questions.stem: What question does a visitor have after the first evening?
reading_questions.explanation: 第二段直接提及访客不了解入口是否有台阶。 原文依据：whether there were steps

reading_questions.stem: What does the revised notice include?
reading_questions.explanation: 新版信息既有地图，也写了闭馆时间。 原文依据：The new notice also stated the closing time

reading_questions.stem: Why can’t the team credit only the new notice for the improvement?
reading_questions.explanation: 团队同时增加志愿者，不能把变化只归因于公告。 原文依据：the extra volunteers may also have helped

reading_questions.stem: What does the team learn about publicity?
reading_questions.explanation: 结尾强调实用信息应与吸引人的设计一样认真规划。 原文依据：useful information should be planned as carefully as an attractive design

reading_questions.stem: How many new books can the class buy?
reading_questions.explanation: 首句写明经费足够购买十二本书。 原文依据：twelve new books

reading_questions.stem: Who supplied most of the first suggestions?
reading_questions.explanation: 第二段说明最初建议主要来自原本就在使用阅读角的学生。 原文依据：students who already used the reading corner

reading_questions.stem: What does the team do with four places on the list?
reading_questions.explanation: 团队预留四个名额满足初始清单遗漏的需求。 原文依据：reserved four places for needs that the first list had missed

reading_questions.stem: Why does the team change the edition of one story?
reading_questions.explanation: 样书试读发现字号太小，所以更换同一故事的版本。 原文依据：print that was too small for comfortable reading

reading_questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
reading_questions.explanation: 结尾强调最积极群体的意见不能代表全班所有需求。 原文依据：rather than a complete picture of what the class needed

reading_questions.stem: Why does the youth group keep a diary?
reading_questions.explanation: 首段指出大家对来源有争议，青年组提议记录而非猜测。 原文依据：keep a diary instead of guessing

reading_questions.stem: What do the volunteers avoid doing?
reading_questions.explanation: 第二段明确不录人声、不拍摄个人。 原文依据：They did not record people's voices

reading_questions.stem: What often happens at the same time?
reading_questions.explanation: 第三段记载卸货与最后一场篮球活动常有重叠。 原文依据：vehicle unloading often overlapped with the final basketball game

reading_questions.stem: Why do volunteers avoid calling the diary precise scientific measurements?
reading_questions.explanation: 原文明确人的主观判断存在差异。 原文依据：different people might judge the same sound differently

reading_questions.stem: Why is another week of notes planned?
reading_questions.explanation: 先调整时间，再记录一周，是为了观察调整后的情况。 原文依据：another week of notes after the changes

reading_questions.stem: What does the first label mainly describe?
reading_questions.explanation: 第一段列出初版标签写了颜色、大小和年代。 原文依据：its colour, size and age

reading_questions.stem: What caused the dent in the lid?
reading_questions.explanation: 捐赠者说明凹痕来自乘公交时摔落，并非学生猜测的工作事故。 原文依据：a fall during a bus journey

reading_questions.stem: How does the group present the memories?
reading_questions.explanation: 第三段说明经同意使用回忆，并明确标示来源。 原文依据：clearly marked the memories as her account

reading_questions.stem: Which claim would the students be least justified in making?
reading_questions.explanation: 原文特别区分实物可证明的信息和个人回忆。 原文依据：did not present every detail as something proved by the object itself

reading_questions.stem: What makes the revised label better?
reading_questions.explanation: 新版加入人物故事，同时没有隐去证据边界。 原文依据：hide the limits of what was known

reading_questions.stem: How much practice does Leo first plan each evening?
reading_questions.explanation: 第一段写他最初每晚安排一小时。 原文依据：an hour of practice

reading_questions.stem: What does Leo tend to avoid during practice?
reading_questions.explanation: 第二段交代他重复简单开头、回避难点。 原文依据：avoided a difficult change between two chords

reading_questions.stem: Why are two evenings left unplanned?
reading_questions.explanation: 留白是为了必要时调整练习时间。 原文依据：so he could move a session when necessary

reading_questions.stem: What does Leo record in his notebook?
reading_questions.explanation: 笔记记录哪些内容变容易、哪些仍需关注。 原文依据：what had become easier and what still needed attention

reading_questions.stem: Which conclusion best matches Leo’s experience?
reading_questions.explanation: 结尾避免一概而论，强调适合当前需求且可持续的计划。 原文依据：matched his present needs and was easier to keep

reading_questions.stem: What was the interview actually about?

reading_questions.stem: How does Mei correct the report?

reading_questions.stem: Why does Mei accept the critical comments?

reading_questions.stem: What checking rule does the team introduce?

reading_questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?

reading_questions.stem: What does the committee first use to judge the route?

reading_questions.stem: What blocks the wheelchair user?

reading_questions.stem: How much extra time does the revised route take?

reading_questions.stem: What lesson does the committee learn?

reading_questions.stem: What is the central message?

reading_questions.stem: What is one cost of Hana’s new approach?

reading_questions.stem: What does the passage encourage?

reading_questions.stem: What is being tested?
reading_questions.explanation: 第一段说明试用的是长椅上方可移动遮阳设施。 原文依据：a movable shade above one courtyard bench

reading_questions.stem: How many visits are recorded in the trial week?
reading_questions.explanation: 第二段给出试用周十八次使用记录。 原文依据：eighteen in the trial week

reading_questions.stem: What weakens a simple claim that the shade caused the entire increase?

reading_questions.stem: What limitation remains after adding another bench for comparison?
reading_questions.explanation: 第三段指出两条长椅位置可能不同。 原文依据：two benches could differ in location

reading_questions.stem: Why is the revised report more useful?
reading_questions.explanation: 报告呈现变化、说明限制，并建议继续试验以支持决策。 原文依据：a clearer basis for its next decision

reading_questions.stem: What problem appears during the first three weekends?
reading_questions.explanation: 首段写可重复使用杯未回到归还区，志愿者需四处寻找。 原文依据：many reusable cups disappeared from the return area

reading_questions.stem: Where is the original return box?
reading_questions.explanation: 第二段明确原归还箱在厨房附近门后。 原文依据：behind a door near the kitchen

reading_questions.stem: Why do organisers follow the cups’ journey?
reading_questions.explanation: 第二段先提出不急于归咎访客，再调查实际使用路径。 原文依据：Instead of assuming visitors did not care

reading_questions.stem: What does the team arrange in addition to better return boxes?
reading_questions.explanation: 第三段说明还需安排清洗所需时间与人员。 原文依据：enough time and staff for washing

reading_questions.stem: What is the main lesson?
reading_questions.explanation: 全文强调重复使用不仅是发出杯子，还需归还和清洗流程。 原文依据：design the return journey with as much care
